title: NDIS Support Worker Salary: Hourly Rates, Annual Pay, and Tax in 2026–27
description: Learn how to calculate an NDIS support worker salary from hourly rates under the SCHADS Award. Includes 38-hour week, casual loading, tax, and super estimates.
salarySummary: An NDIS support worker on the SCHADS Award Level 3 pay point earns a minimum hourly rate that is the standard rate for allowances; annual pay is hourly rate × 38 hours × 52 weeks, with super and tax estimated separately.

faqs.q: What is the minimum hourly rate for an NDIS support worker under the SCHADS Award?
faqs.a: The SCHADS Award sets minimum pay rates for social and community services employees, including disability support workers. The exact rate depends on the classification level and pay point. For example, the sleepover allowance is calculated as 4.9% of the standard rate for a Level 3 pay point 3 employee. For current minimum rates, use the Fair Work Ombudsman’s Pay and Conditions Tool or download the SCHADS Award pay guide.

faqs.q: How is casual loading applied to NDIS support worker pay?
faqs.a: Casual employees under the SCHADS Award receive a 25% loading on top of the minimum hourly rate. This loading is included in the casual rates shown in the NDIS Pricing Schedule. When using a calculator, you can add the 25% loading separately rather than typing a rate that already includes it.

faqs.q: What tax and super contributions apply to an NDIS support worker salary?
faqs.a: For 2026–27, resident tax rates are: nil up to $18,200; 15% from $18,201 to $45,000; 30% to $135,000; 37% to $190,000; 45% above that. Medicare levy is generally 2%. Super guarantee is 12% of ordinary earnings, paid on top, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. These are estimates; use the ATO’s tax withheld calculator for precise figures.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the NDIS Support Worker Salary

An **NDIS support worker salary** is typically based on the Social, Community, Home Care and Disability Services Industry Award (SCHADS Award). This award covers employees providing disability support services under the National Disability Insurance Scheme. The Fair Work Ombudsman explains that full-time employees work 38 hours per week, arranged as 5 shifts of 8 hours, or by agreement up to 10 or 12 hours for sleepover shifts.

### Award Rates vs. NDIS Pricing Schedule

The SCHADS Award sets minimum pay rates for each classification level. The NDIS Pricing Schedule 2026–27 published by the NDIA provides maximum prices that providers can charge participants, not necessarily the salary an employee receives. For example, a Disability Support Worker Level 1 has a weekday daytime rate of $73.58 per hour under the Pricing Schedule, but the actual award rate may be lower. Always refer to the Fair Work Ombudsman’s tools for the correct minimum wage.

## How to Calculate Annual Pay from an Hourly Rate

To estimate your annual **NDIS support worker salary**, use the formula:

**Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

We assume a standard 38-hour week for full-time employees. For part-time or casual workers, adjust the hours accordingly.

### Example Calculation

If your hourly rate under the SCHADS Award is $30.00 (hypothetical), your annual gross pay would be:

$30.00 × 38 × 52 = $59,280

For a fortnightly figure, multiply weekly pay by 2:

Weekly pay = $30.00 × 38 = $1,140
Fortnightly pay = $1,140 × 2 = $2,280

### Casual Loading

Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the minimum hourly rate. For example, if the base rate is $30.00, the casual rate is $37.50. When using [the timesheet](/), check the box to add 25% casual loading – do not type a rate that already includes it.

## Tax and Super on Your NDIS Support Worker Salary

### Income Tax (2026–27 Resident Rates)

| Taxable Income | Tax on this income |
| --- | --- |
| $0 – $18,200 | Nil |
| $18,201 – $45,000 | 15c for each $1 over $18,200 |
| $45,001 – $135,000 | $4,020 plus 30c for each $1 over $45,000 |
| $135,001 – $190,000 | $31,020 plus 37c for each $1 over $135,000 |
| Over $190,000 | $51,370 plus 45c for each $1 over $190,000 |

Plus Medicare levy of 2% (based on 2025–26 single reduction thresholds).

### Super Guarantee

Your employer must pay superannuation of 12% on your ordinary earnings, on top of your salary. This is capped at the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. For an annual salary of $59,280, super would be $7,113.60 paid into your fund.

## Using the Timesheet Tool

Our [the timesheet](/) lets you enter your base hourly rate and optionally add casual loading. It calculates annual gross pay, tax, Medicare, and super. For more detailed pay guides, visit [pay guides](/blog).

### Important Notes

- This calculation assumes the same rate every week with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances.
- Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top.
- Tax uses the 2026–27 resident scale with full tax-free threshold.
- This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

For exact award rates, use the Fair Work Ombudsman’s Pay and Conditions Tool. For tax advice, consult the Australian Taxation Office.
